item.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fusion power plants will need a lot of lithium, and Licube is preparing to be a key supplier.

item.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The San Francisco startup aims to help battery and chip manufacturers identify defects on production lines, reducing downtime and costly mistakes.

item.title: Rivian spinoff Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec, Sean O'Kane
item.description: Field also worked on Apple's secretive car project and oversaw development of the Tesla Model 3.

item.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

item.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

item.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality.

item.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

item.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

item.title: MIT startup says it can turn diesel trucks into cheaper hydrogen haulers — see it at Disrupt
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Diesel is expensive and polluting, and LNK Energies says it has come up with a way to replace it with hydrogen, all while undercutting diesel on cost.

item.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is making it easier to build and use personal Android apps created with AI, without having to make them available to everyone on the Play Store.

item.title: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.

item.title: The 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20: From organs to orbit and everything in between
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Johannessen
item.description: Twenty founders just earned their shot at Disrupt glory. They're headed to the main stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to compete for the $100,000 prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.

item.title: Spotify users on iOS 27 can now ask Siri to play music without having to say ‘on Spotify’
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Siri can now learn users' preferred music app, allowing Spotify listeners to request songs, podcasts, and playlists without specifying which app to use.

item.title: Bumble agrees to a $1.3B acquisition deal as online dating faces a reset
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: After years of declining subscriber numbers and falling revenue, Bumble just agreed to a $1.3 billion acquisition.

item.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 1
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 officially kicks off today. See what's in store for Day 1 (Oct. 13) at San Francisco's Moscone West. Don't miss it. Register for your pass now and meet 10,000+ tech leaders at the startup epicenter of the year.

item.title: SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The new X Subscription combines X's paid features with AI tools like Grok and Cursor, offering plans ranging from $8 to $200 per month.

item.title: Apple refreshes its HomePod mini with a new chip and $149 price tag
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: The new $149 HomePod mini with Siri AI and a 'SoundGlow' visual feature will be available starting October 30.

item.title: Apple’s new smart home lineup includes a smart lock, thermostat, and video doorbells
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The new devices work with HomeView, the company's new smart home hub which can be used to control accessories and interact with apps.

item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: The full TechCrunch Disrupt Stage lineup revealed, featuring Max Hodak, Mark Wahlberg, Benchmark partners, and more. Register now to save up to $100 on your pass and get a second at 50% off.

item.title: India delays digital payments fee rollout amid retailer pushback
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: The NPCI, which operates the UPI network, said it was postponing the planned October 15 rollout of the 0.4% fee due to the festive shopping season.
